title: Trigonometry: SOHCAHTOA (KS4)
subject: Maths
strapline: Finding missing sides and angles in right-angled triangles.
facts: Label the sides relative to the angle: opposite (facing it), adjacent (next to it), hypotenuse (longest, opposite the right angle).
SOHCAHTOA: Sin = Opp/Hyp, Cos = Adj/Hyp, Tan = Opp/Adj.
Choose the ratio that uses the two sides/angle you know and want.
To find a side, multiply; e.g. opp = hyp × sin(angle).
To find an angle, use the inverse function on your calculator: angle = sin⁻¹(opp/hyp).
Make sure your calculator is in degrees mode for GCSE work.
Trigonometry, like Pythagoras, only works on right-angled triangles at this level.

quick_quiz.q: Which ratio uses opposite and adjacent?
To find an unknown angle from two sides, what do you use?
quick_quiz.a: the inverse function (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹)

teacher_tips: Label opp/adj/hyp first, every time, before choosing a ratio.
Check calculators are in degrees — a classic silent error.
Separate "finding a side" (multiply) from "finding an angle" (inverse).
